Section 1370(a)(2) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
    (1) in subparagraph (E)—
        (A) by inserting “(i)” after “exceed”; and 
        (B) by inserting before the period at the end the following: “or (ii) in the case of officers of that armed force in a grade specified in subparagraph (G), two officers, whichever number is greater”; and  
    (2) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(G) Notwithstanding subparagraph (E), during fiscal years 2013 through 2017, the total number of brigadier generals and major generals of the Army, Air Force, and Marine Corps, and the total number of rear admirals (lower half) and rear admirals of the Navy, for whom a reduction is made under this section during any fiscal year of service-in-grade otherwise required under this paragraph may not exceed 10 percent of the authorized active-duty strength for that fiscal year for officers of that armed force in those grades.”.

fable.w: This section amends 10 U.S.C. 1370 to set numerical caps on how many general and flag officers may receive a reduction in the service-in-grade requirement for retirement. It is a purely internal military personnel rule: no outside party is consulted, no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or advisory body is created, and no right to sue is granted. There is no real tempting reading beyond the procedural tone, and every actor involved is inside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the U.S. Code to set numerical limits on the reduction of military officers. It involves internal personnel management and statutory caps within the Department of Defense. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities such as the public, states, or private organizations.
qwen_block.s: Section 1370(a)(2) of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) in subparagraph (E)— (A) by inserting “(i)” after “exceed”; and (B) by inserting before the period at the end the following: “or (ii) in the case of officers of that armed force in a grade specified in subparagraph (G), two officers, whichever number is greater”; and (2) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(G) Notwithstanding subparagraph (E), during fiscal years 2013 through 2017, the total number of brigadier generals and major generals of the Army, Air Force, and Marine Corps, and the total number of rear admirals (lower half) and rear admirals of the Navy, for whom a reduction is made under this section during any fiscal year of service-in-grade otherwise required under this paragraph may not exceed 10 percent of the authorized active-duty strength for that fiscal year for officers of that armed force in those grades.”.

opus.w: This provision only changes numerical caps on how many general and flag officers can have their service-in-grade requirements reduced under 10 U.S.C. 1370. It has no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue that involves anyone outside the federal government. Military officers and the armed forces are inside the federal government, so even the personnel decisions it touches stay internal.
opus.b:
The section changes caps on how many general and flag officers can have their service-in-grade requirements reduced. No outside party is involved.

1. **Tempting reading:** Words like "authorized" and "reduction" could suggest a decision process, and nothing here mentions consultation, hearings, rulemaking or a right to sue. The only actors are the armed forces and their officers, who are all inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the U.S. Code to set limits on the number of high-ranking military officers (brigadier generals, major generals, rear admirals) who can be reduced in grade. Military officers are federal employees, and this provision concerns internal personnel management and statutory caps on force structure. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation with any entity outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private companies).
qwen_chat.s: Section 1370(a)(2) of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) in subparagraph (E)— (A) by inserting “(i)” after “exceed”; and (B) by inserting before the period at the end the following: “or (ii) in the case of officers of that armed force in a grade specified in subparagraph (G), two officers, whichever number is greater”; and (2) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(G) Notwithstanding subparagraph (E), during fiscal years 2013 through 2017, the total number of brigadier generals and major generals of the Army, Air Force, and Marine Corps, and the total number of rear admirals (lower half) and rear admirals of the Navy, for whom a reduction is made under this section during any fiscal year of service-in-grade otherwise required under this paragraph may not exceed 10 percent of the authorized active-duty strength for that fiscal year for officers of that armed force in those grades.”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the amendment involves "participation" because it changes rules regarding military officers, who are people. However, military officers are federal employees, and changes to their personnel limits are internal government management decisions, not interactions with outside parties.
